body.name: Finite-grid population profile
body.construction: Specialize the moving-cutoff family to \(\kappa_n=1/32\) and \(t=0\). Take \(\mathcal G_c=\{3/8,1/2,5/8\}\), \(\mathcal G_\vartheta=\{-1,0,1\}\), and the four-bin partition \([0,3/8),[3/8,1/2),[1/2,5/8),[5/8,1]\). In the cell order \((0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), the bin-average joint-cell vectors, each divided by \(8192\), are \[(1947,2277,1829,2139),\quad(2079,2145,1953,2015),\quad(1953,2015,2079,2145),\quad(1829,2139,1947,2277).\] Every vector is nonnegative and sums to one. Their treatment margins are \(31/64\) in the first two bins and \(33/64\) in the last two; their outcome margins equal \(69/128,65/128,65/128,69/128\). The unrestricted association coordinate is the displayed fourth cell in each bin. The true pair \((c,\vartheta)=(1/2,0)\) belongs to the profile domain and has population deviance zero. For this four-bin, three-by-three grid, the finite-sample threshold is \(3\sum_{k=1}^4\log(N_k(1/2)+1)+\log(9/\delta_n)\). A certified infeasible null is rejected. The rule returns \(\Theta\) under each and only each of the following fallback branches: a bin required by the certificate is empty; cutoff-grid enlargement is uncertified; effect-grid enlargement is uncertified; the inner--outer H\"older gap exceeds \(M b_n^s\); the solver fails; the reported optimum lacks a certificate; the projected treatment-jump confidence set meets \([0,\kappa_n/2]\); the universal threshold cannot be computed; or the requested \(n\), grid, or sieve is outside the deterministic schedule. Ties are resolved lexicographically.
